chapter: Lee Collins and the riverboat Washington
title: Canal Street gigs and his United Food day job
summary: He worked Canal Street and kept a day job at United Food Company.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: What about Coyne? What were you doing in those days when the jittery lad was going, like in the Coyne?
Well, I worked, I worked on Canal Street a while, um, Madden Gabriel. I worked at them a while with a, with Zev and different guys like that. Did you have a day job too?

I worked there a while. See, cause I wouldn't work, you know, like alternate, like, God won't get off two nights or something like that, you know. I'd work like that. All the more penitentiary jobs, I didn't even need the college jobs. That's right, penitentiary. Yeah. I worked on them guys. I used to like to be with them cause you know, they drink, you know. Like guys, he worked with them either. We'd be together every day, every morning, guys would be looking for me, you know. Well I was with good guys all the time, well they was teaching me all the time, you understand. They didn't play my instrument, but I was playing enough at that time for anybody. I could sit in anybody's band around here, you understand. But I was playing, I knew more, listen, I was playing better music than a lot of them was playing in bands and I wasn't playing with nobody. I was working for a food company, you understand. That's the truth.
